item.title: [ABC Action News / Tampa Bay 28] US bans foreign-made humanoid robots, targeting China over national security
item.description: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission is banning imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots and power inverters, citing national security risks, in a move that targets China. Beijing quickly accused the U.S. of protectionism.

item.title: [ABC Action News / Tampa Bay 28] FIFA's Infantino sets deadline to members in Kushner-backed World Cup plan
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino set a Sept. 19 deadline on Wednesday for the 211 member federations to accept one-off $20 million offers as part of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

item.title: [ABC Action News / Tampa Bay 28] Flooding spreads in eastern New York as the heavy rain responsible shifts to New England
item.description: Dangerous flooding is unfolding in eastern New York amid torrential rainfall as a band of slow-moving downpours move toward New England after drenching New Jersey and Pennsylvania on Tuesday.

item.title: [ABC Action News / Tampa Bay 28] Iran resumes attacks as US-Saudi strikes kill Tehran-backed militants in Iraq
item.description: Iran launched missiles at U.S. troops Wednesday as American and Saudi forces struck Tehran-backed militants in Iraq, killing at least 20, raising fears of a return to full-scale war.

item.title: [ABC Action News / Tampa Bay 28] 'Once' Oscar winner and Irish musician Glen Hansard dies in motorcycle crash
item.description: Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard, who won an Academy Award for the 2007 film “Once,” died in a motorcycle crash on the outskirts of Dublin early Wednesday, his management said. He was 56.
